title: Road Traffic
Accident
Rehabilitation
hero.text: For patients recovering from road traffic accidents and other traumatic injuries, to rebuild physical function and return to everyday life.

overview: Road traffic accident rehabilitation is a structured recovery pathway designed to help individuals regain physical, cognitive and emotional function following traumatic injury caused by motor vehicle accidents. These incidents can result in complex injuries, ranging from fractures and soft tissue damage to traumatic brain injuries, which may require ongoing rehabilitation beyond emergency treatment.

topics.label: What Is Road Traffic Accident Rehabilitation?

blocks.text: Road traffic accident rehabilitation is specialised care that helps patients recover following injuries caused by motor vehicle accidents. After emergency treatment, patients receive structured rehabilitation to restore physical and cognitive function and regain the skills needed for everyday life.

topics.label: Injuries We Help Patients Recover From

items: Serious injuries such as traumatic brain injury, skull fractures and other significant trauma
After emergency treatment, which may include surgery, a dedicated rehabilitation team helps patients relearn everyday abilities and return to independent life

blocks.text: Occupational therapy helps patients rebuild the skills they need for everyday life and work, from managing daily activities to typing, handwriting, reading and preparing to return to the workplace with confidence.
Occupational therapy can also support cognitive recovery by helping patients improve attention and memory, regain everyday function.

Physical rehabilitation helps patients recover from the physical effects of trauma, including persistent pain in the spine, muscles, bones or limbs, difficulty with movement or coordination, dizziness, balance problems and physical fatigue

Physiotherapy uses targeted exercises and rehabilitation techniques to improve strength, mobility, balance and physical function. Treatment may be supported by appropriate pain management, nutrition, rest and specialised equipment where required.

Early intervention matters: timely therapy can help prevent or reduce the risk of long-term complications such as chronic pain and recurring headaches, and support the recovery of basic functions like walking and eating independently.

Speech and language therapy helps patients regain communication skills that may have been affected by a traumatic brain injury or other neurological injury. Depending on the patient’s needs, therapy may address speech, language, communication, swallowing or related difficulties.

Speech and language therapy can also support patients experiencing hearing difficulties, through tailored exercises and, where appropriate, assistive devices. The treatment plan is always guided by the individual’s needs and progress.
